headline: If crossfire is necessary and the government allows it, we will do it: IGP

members.title: If crossfire is necessary and the government allows it, we will do it: IGP
members.lead: Inspector General of Police (IGP) Md Ali Hossain Fakir has said police will resort to “crossfire” if necessary, provided the government gives permission. He made the remarks while speaking as the chief guest at the inauguration of Community Islamic, the Islamic banking service of Community Bank Bangladesh PLC, in Chawkbazar, Old Dhaka, on Monday afternoon. IGP Ali Hossain Fakir said police are labelled fascist when they use force, while they are called weak when they remain inactive. The police must be provided with a suitable environment to perform their duties and maintain law and order, he said. “Where crossfire is necessary, if the government allows it, we will do it,” he said. . Referring to criticism of police conduct and the use of force, the IGP said, “When police baton-charge people, they are called fascist. But when police remain silent, they are called weak. Under these circumstances, the police must be given an environment in which they can work and be equipped to carry out their responsibilities.” The IGP said the law and the Constitution must be followed to maintain peace and order in society. Police must take action against crimes, and members of the force must also face action if they commit offences, he added. He also stressed the need for public cooperation in maintaining law and order. He said it was important to verify facts rather than be misled by rumours and misinformation. Collective cooperation from all concerned was necessary to maintain normalcy in the law and order situation and ensure the country's economic progress, the IGP said.

members.title: TIB calls for withdrawal of IGP’s remarks and accountability
members.lead: Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) in a statement on Monday strongly condemned and expressed deep concern over the Inspector General of Police’s (IGP) remarks that the police would resort to crossfire, if necessary, to maintain law and order, provided the government gives its approval. According to TIB, the remarks send a dangerous message by presenting extrajudicial killings as an acceptable means of crime control, rather than addressing failures in maintaining law and order and institutional weaknesses. Describing the remarks as an expression of utter disregard for the Constitution and the rule of law, TIB has demanded their immediate withdrawal, accountability of the IGP, and accountability for making a declaration that contradicts the government’s stated position against extrajudicial killings. . TIB Executive Director Iftekharuzzaman said, “Is the police chief seeking to use the discredited practice of crossfire as a shield for the police’s failure to maintain law and order? Does seeking to legitimise extrajudicial killings by making them conditional on government approval amount to an admission of failure to combat crime through lawful means?" "The responsibility of the police is to conduct professional investigations, identify offenders and bring the accused to trial on the basis of admissible evidence. Presenting crossfire as an alternative cannot resolve institutional weaknesses; rather, it is an example of professional bankruptcy," the TIB executive director added. Iftekharuzzaman pointed out, "In the same remarks, the IGP spoke of discharging duties in accordance with the law and the Constitution, while also saying that the police would resort to crossfire if the government approved it. These two positions are contradictory. No government approval can legitimise an extrajudicial killing. The rights to legal protection and to life and personal liberty guaranteed under Articles 31 and 32 of the Constitution cannot be set aside by executive decision…
